Frequently Asked Questions About Wrinkle Treatment
How much do wrinkle treatments cost?

The cost of a wrinkle treatment varies depending on the method and treatment area. A wrinkle injection with hyaluronic acid or botulinum toxin typically starts at around €200. More complex procedures such as thread lifting or PRP treatment may incur higher costs.
After a personal consultation—during which we determine the optimal treatment together—you’ll receive a transparent and detailed cost breakdown from KU64, of course.
Which wrinkle treatment lasts the longest?
How long the results of a wrinkle treatment last depends on various factors, especially the chosen method. Individual factors like your skin type and metabolism also play a role.
Unlike plastic surgery, non- or minimally invasive treatments do not provide permanent results. However, they are gentle and require no extended recovery time.
Botulinum toxin reduces expression lines for about 3 to 6 months, while a wrinkle injection with hyaluronic acid can last between 6 and 18 months, depending on the treated area.
Thread lifting offers even longer-lasting results, as it stimulates the body’s natural collagen production and can sustainably improve skin structure—for up to 2 years.

A particularly long-lasting option is autologous fat injections , which use the patient’s own fat—usually harvested via liposuction—to fill wrinkles. This method can deliver years of results by strengthening the skin structure and rejuvenating your complexion. A non-invasive laser treatment can also improve skin texture over the long term.
Our specialists will gladly advise you in detail on which treatment best suits your goals and how to achieve a natural, long-lasting result.
Can I get liposuction on my face?

Facial liposuction is technically possible but usually not the first choice for facial contouring. A gentler alternative is the fat-dissolving injection (injection lipolysis), which selectively breaks down fat cells and helps the body eliminate them naturally. This method is especially suitable for smaller fat deposits, such as on the cheeks or chin.
As an additional wrinkle treatment, options like wrinkle injections or laser treatments can further tighten the skin and refine facial contours.
Feel free to contact us for a personal consultation to find out which method is best for you and your individual needs!
[ Smooth away frown lines for a relaxed and youthful appearance ]

Glabellar lines – also known as frown lines – are the vertical wrinkles that form between the eyebrows. They often appear when we frown or concentrate, but over time, they can become permanent even when the face is at rest. At KU64, we offer gentle and effective treatments to reduce these expression lines and restore a relaxed, youthful facial expression.
From Glabellar Lines to Crow’s Feet: Why Do Wrinkles Form?

Every wrinkle tells a story—of laughter, deep thought, sunny days, or moments of stress. At some point, we notice that these lines remain even when our face is relaxed and deepen over time. While some people see the first signs of wrinkles in their twenties, others maintain firm, youthful skin well into their forties. But why is that? Let’s take a look at the causes.
Facial expressions, stress, and natural aging

Every time we laugh or squint, our facial muscles contract. Over the years, these micro-movements leave marks on the skin. The forehead is particularly affected, as we tend to use these muscles frequently. Alongside horizontal forehead lines, the glabellar lines are often among the first to appear visibly.

As we age, the skin’s production of collagen and elastin—proteins responsible for firmness and elasticity—slows down. As these components break down, the skin can no longer fully smooth out after facial movements. Fine lines that initially appeared only with certain expressions eventually become permanent.

Stress can accelerate this process. Those under constant tension often furrow their brows or frown—a habit that deepens glabellar lines over time. In addition, stress hormones like cortisol further reduce collagen and elastin and impair the skin’s regenerative ability.
Genetics and environmental influences

Alongside facial expressions and the natural aging process, genetics also play a major role in wrinkle formation. Some people naturally have thicker, more resilient skin that resists deep lines for longer. Others have a finer, more delicate skin structure that shows signs of aging earlier. A genetic predisposition to lower collagen production can also lead to earlier wrinkling—even with excellent skincare and a healthy lifestyle.

But it’s not just genes—external factors also significantly influence how quickly wrinkles develop. One of the leading causes of premature aging is UV exposure. It accelerates the breakdown of collagen and elastin, causing the skin to lose firmness. UV rays also damage both the skin barrier and deeper layers, impairing the skin’s ability to regenerate. So the best tip for slowing skin aging? Use sunscreen daily!
Other factors such as pollution, lack of sleep, and poor nutrition can also rob the skin of its glow. Free radicals from exhaust fumes and environmental toxins attack skin cells and speed up aging.

So while many factors contribute to wrinkle formation, the good news is that many of them are within your control. And there’s even better news: Thanks to modern aesthetic treatments like targeted botulinum toxin applications, wrinkles can be significantly reduced.
Remove Glabellar Lines & More Wrinkle Treatments at KU64 Berlin

Not a fan of that stern or tired look in the mirror that doesn’t match how you actually feel? If you’d like to smooth your forehead or other facial areas without undergoing plastic surgery or a forehead lift, aesthetic medicine offers a range of non-invasive and minimally invasive options.
Botulinum toxin – the most effective solution for a smooth forehead

When it comes to treating forehead wrinkles—especially glabellar lines—botulinum toxin (Botox) is often the treatment of choice. It relaxes the muscles responsible for wrinkle formation, allowing the skin to smooth out while also preventing further lines from developing. The key advantage: with the right dosage, your natural facial expressions are preserved. Only the constant unconscious muscle tension that causes the wrinkles is reduced.

The effects of botulinum toxin begin within the first few days after treatment and are fully visible within a week. Soon, your forehead appears more relaxed, your glabellar lines are visibly reduced, and your overall expression looks softer and more refreshed. As the body breaks down the substance slowly, results typically last three to six months. After that, the treatment can easily be repeated.

Another advantage of minimally invasive wrinkle treatments like botulinum toxin injections: unlike plastic surgery, there’s no extended recovery or downtime. After a short period of rest, you can return to your daily routine right away.
Other Treatments for Forehead Wrinkles: Hyaluronic Acid, Laser & More – A Comparison

Looking for plumping rather than muscle relaxation? Hyaluronic acid may be a great alternative. This naturally occurring substance binds moisture and adds volume under the skin. For deep-set wrinkles, a combination of botulinum toxin and hyaluronic acid often delivers the best results.

Modern laser treatments are another option to reduce wrinkles. They stimulate natural collagen production and enhance the skin’s texture in the long term. However, several sessions are usually required for visible results.

If you’re seeking a long-term solution, plastic surgery might be the answer. However, procedures like a forehead lift involve more effort, higher risks, and longer recovery periods. That’s why it’s essential to receive thorough consultation and guidance from your medical professional.

Ultimately, the best treatment for wrinkles depends on the results you’re looking for and how much time and budget you’re willing to invest in treatment and recovery. During a personal consultation, we’ll help you find the solution that fits your needs best.
Why Botulinum Toxin Is So Popular for Treating Glabellar Lines

Botulinum toxin is a go-to for both doctors and patients when it comes to wrinkle treatment—especially for removing glabellar lines. It’s an effective and well-established solution for treating forehead lines and frown lines alike.
How does botulinum toxin work?

Glabellar lines and horizontal forehead wrinkles are primarily caused by overactive muscles in the forehead or between the eyebrows. Repeated frowning—whether due to stress, concentration, or habit—causes the skin to fold in the same spots again and again. Over time, these lines remain visible even when the face is at rest.

This is exactly where botulinum toxin comes in: it blocks the communication between nerves and muscles in a targeted way. The treated muscles relax, and the overlying skin smooths out. That makes it a highly effective treatment for reducing or even removing glabellar lines.
The Treatment – Quick, Precise, and Gentle
A wrinkle treatment with botulinum toxin usually takes just 15 to 20 minutes. After analyzing your facial muscles, the substance is injected into the targeted areas using a fine needle.

At KU64 Berlin, we place great importance on precise dosing and application. That’s how our doctors achieve natural-looking results: your forehead won’t look stiff—it’ll appear relaxed and visibly smoother.
Results: When will I see an effect, and how long does it last?

Changes become visible within three to four days after treatment. About a week after your botulinum toxin injection, the full effect sets in: your glabellar lines appear smoothed, and your overall facial expression looks softer and more relaxed.

Depending on individual factors like metabolism, skin type, and lifestyle, the results of a botulinum toxin treatment usually last between three and six months. With regular touch-ups, the effect can be maintained long-term—preventing deep wrinkles from reappearing.
Total relaxation: More aesthetic treatments with botulinum toxin

Treating glabellar lines is one of the most common uses for botulinum toxin—but by far not the only one. Whether forehead wrinkles, crow’s feet, or downturned corners of the mouth, many signs of skin aging can be gently corrected with botulinum toxin—without compromising your natural facial expressions. Fine lines can be reduced, facial features harmonized, and even certain muscle tensions targeted.
Gentle smoothing of forehead lines and crow’s feet

It’s not just glabellar lines—your entire forehead is one of the most expressive areas of the face. Whether you’re raising your eyebrows or concentrating deeply, this area is under constant strain. Over time, this leads to horizontal lines across the forehead: the classic forehead wrinkles.
Our facial expressions also cause so-called crow’s feet—the fine lines at the outer corners of the eyes. These become especially visible when smiling or squinting and tend to deepen with age.

Botulinum toxin specifically relaxes the muscles in these areas, allowing the skin above to smooth out. The result: your forehead appears more rested, the eye area looks fresher, and your entire face gains a relaxed, youthful appearance.
Softening lip lines and lifting corners of the mouth—for a radiant smile

Fine lines around the lips tend to develop in people with expressive facial movements and naturally thinner skin. Smokers are especially prone to vertical lines above the upper lip—commonly known as smoker’s lines.
As we age, the corners of the mouth may also begin to turn slightly downward. Many of our patients feel this makes them appear grumpy or unhappy—even when they’re not.

With precise botulinum toxin injections, these lines around the mouth and lips can be softened, and the corners of the mouth gently lifted. The result is a more positive, open smile—without compromising your natural expression.
Gummy smile, masseter & more—botulinum toxin for a balanced facial profile

In addition to wrinkle-smoothing treatments, botulinum toxin has several lesser-known yet highly effective aesthetic applications. One of these is correcting a gummy smile —where too much gum is visible when smiling. By gently relaxing specific muscles, the balance between lips and teeth can be harmonized for a more attractive smile.

Botulinum toxin can also be used to subtly reshape the face. For those bothered by a prominent jaw muscle (masseter), targeted injections can relax the area, resulting in a slimmer and softer lower face—ideal for anyone seeking a more contoured jawline.

This makes botulinum toxin a highly versatile treatment. Whether you’re aiming for more refined facial features, a fresher appearance, or more harmonious proportions, botulinum toxin offers a gentle but effective alternative to plastic surgery. Our specialists are happy to advise you on which treatment is best suited to achieve your desired result.
Safety and Tolerability of Botulinum Toxin

If you’re considering an aesthetic treatment with botulinum toxin, you’re likely wondering about its safety. After all, it’s a substance that specifically relaxes muscles—an intervention in your body’s natural function.

As with any medical treatment, there’s a potential for side effects. The good news: botulinum toxin has been used for decades in both aesthetic and medical treatments and is considered one of the safest and best-tolerated methods for wrinkle reduction—when administered professionally and in appropriate doses.
Side effects and risks of botulinum toxin

Botulinum toxin is injected in minimal amounts and remains active only in the treated area. Severe side effects are extremely rare. However, as with any injection, temporary reactions may occur—such as slight redness, swelling, or small bruises at the injection site. These typically disappear within a few days.

In rare cases, there may be temporary weakening of nearby muscles. This can cause slight drooping of the eyebrows or an asymmetrical appearance. Such effects are not permanent, as the body breaks down the substance completely within a few months.

To ensure the best results, it’s important to follow certain aftercare guidelines: avoid intense physical activity, direct sun exposure, and sauna visits for a few days after treatment. This allows the substance to distribute properly and unfold its full effect in the muscles.
At KU64 in Berlin, our experienced doctors will inform you in detail about all possible risks and answer any questions you may have. Feel free to contact us for an initial consultation!
Is Botulinum Toxin Right for Me?

In general, botulinum toxin is suitable for most people who want to reduce wrinkles gently or refine certain facial features. However, treatment is not recommended in certain cases. We advise against it if you:
are pregnant or breastfeeding
have a neuromuscular disorder affecting muscle activity
are allergic to any ingredient in the injection
If none of these apply to you, botulinum toxin is a safe and well-tolerated method when administered by a trained professional—to smooth wrinkles and relax your facial expression.

eintraege.h1: Bone augmentation for dental implants in the jaw

bloecke.text: Sinus Lift and Bone Grafting for a Dental Implant

For the successful, long-lasting placement of dental implants, sufficient bone volume is essential. In general, the stronger the bone, the better the support for the implant. However, if the bone does not meet the necessary requirements, its quality in the jawbone or sinus area can be improved before the actual implantation through various bone augmentation techniques, such as a sinus lift. The effort and cost involved in these procedures can vary significantly.

Bone loss in the jaw is usually caused by periodontitis, tooth loss, or the high chewing pressure on the sinus floor from a dental prosthesis. Other factors, such as genetics, general medical conditions, medication use, age, and habits like smoking, can also influence the extent of bone loss.
Bone Augmentation for a Dental Implant: Requirements

For optimal stability of dental implants, sufficient bone height and, depending on the implant, adequate bone width in the jaw are essential. Reconstructing bone width is generally less challenging than increasing bone height.

In the lower jaw, bone density and quality are typically higher than in the upper jaw, which increases the chances of successful implantation. In the upper jaw, however, the protruding maxillary sinus often leaves insufficient natural bone to securely anchor a dental implant. In such cases, a procedure known as a sinus lift can provide the necessary bone support.
External Sinus Lift & Internal Sinus Lift
A sinus lift generally refers to the surgical thickening or elevation of the sinus floor, with two main types distinguished: external (lateral) and internal (crestal) sinus lifts.

A sinus lift can only be performed in the upper jaw, where either the patient’s own bone or bone substitute material is surgically placed beneath the maxillary sinus. This creates increased bone height, which after a healing period of approximately 4 months provides sufficient support for a dental implant.

The external sinus lift is the more complex procedure, used when the existing bone height is very low and several millimeters of additional bone height need to be gained. This requires precise and careful exposure of the sinus wall to insert the bone material into the space between the sinus membrane and the bone.

The internal sinus lift is a minimally invasive procedure where access to the sinus floor is gained through the implant’s osteotomy (drilling) site. The advantage is that no second surgical site needs to be opened. However, this method also requires patience and high precision, especially since visibility through the small drilling hole can be limited.

bloecke.text: Artificial tooth roots that function like your own teeth
You are currently viewing a placeholder content from YouTube . To access the actual content, click the button below. Please note that doing so will share data with third-party providers.

When a tooth is lost, it often affects not only our health but also our quality of life. With a dental implant, missing teeth, bridges, or even entire rows of teeth can be replaced — permanently. At KU64 Berlin, our specialists support you with high-quality tooth replacements on your journey to a confident, aesthetic smile and greater joy in life.
Dental Implants Berlin – NEW Roots FOR Strong Teeth Instead OF Dentures

Whether due to tooth migration, a broken tooth, or aesthetic concerns — the reasons for needing a replacement are as varied as the restoration options themselves. Professional dental implants are the most advanced form of tooth replacement in modern dentistry and can provide a long-term solution for individual or multiple missing teeth. For example, a single gap can be closed with a “new” tooth — without grinding down neighboring healthy teeth for a bridge. Aesthetics and natural chewing comfort are fully preserved. Dental implants are an optimal solution for regaining quality of life without gaps in your smile.

The implantology team at KU64 in Berlin-Charlottenburg delivers long-lasting results at the highest standard, thanks to cutting-edge technology and techniques, and a team of highly qualified oral and maxillofacial surgeons and implantologists.

Implants can also enhance existing dentures or ensure that a prosthesis is securely anchored. In many cases, thanks to what’s known as „additional support," classic dentures can be avoided entirely. The palate remains free from plastic or metal, and the securely anchored teeth allow for confident chewing, biting, and smiling.
Benefits OF Dental Implants
A dental implant looks and functions like a natural tooth.
Implants allow for much stronger biting than dentures and often make chewing easier.
Professional implants preserve speech or even improve it compared to other tooth replacements.
Unlike many bridges and dentures, implants help prevent bone loss in the jaw.
Neighboring teeth remain intact when implants are placed.
Implants cannot develop cavities.
Artificial tooth roots (implants) can stabilize removable dentures or support fixed bridges.
Long-lasting AND Stable: OUR Implant Materials

Today, most dental implants are made from titanium, as this material bonds best with bone. Titanium is well-researched, highly durable, and entirely biocompatible. Our implants come from leading manufacturers and feature a special bioactive surface to further accelerate healing.

Other materials, like zirconia, are also used. Zirconia is a ceramic material known for its high biocompatibility and is primarily used in dental restorations. These ceramic implants offer superior aesthetics and a particularly natural appearance.
Implant Procedure AT OUR Berlin Practice

Ideally, the implant is placed shortly after the gentle removal of a tooth. Precondition: the teeth, gums, and surrounding structures — in short, everything around the implant site — must be in a healthy condition. There’s little benefit in placing an expensive implant if gum disease or a lack of preventive care compromises long-term success. These factors should always be evaluated before treatment.
As a rule: the stronger the bone, the better the implant holds in the jaw.
Sinus lift: Bone augmentation for stable roots

Often, small bone deficiencies — such as a very thin jawbone — must be corrected in advance using the patient’s own bone or substitute materials. This is called bone augmentation. In this context, the term “sinus lift” is frequently used.
Placing the implant

To insert the implant after successful bone augmentation, the gum is carefully detached from the jaw at the planned site. A socket matching the exact shape of the implant is drilled into the bone, and the implant is screwed in. Finally, the gum is sutured, and healing begins.

Apart from a slight wound sensation, pain is usually manageable with mild painkillers. Depending on the extent of the procedure, swelling and bruising may occur during the first postoperative week. Over time, the implant bonds with the jawbone (osseointegration), which takes about eight weeks in the lower jaw and approximately twelve weeks in the upper jaw — with individual differences.
Attaching the dental restoration

In the third step, the implant is exposed again and the final tooth replacement is attached to the artificial root. This may be a single ceramic crown, a bridge, or a denture. Sometimes, several implants are connected with a bar onto which the denture is placed.
HOW Bone Augmentation Works

Thanks to modern oral surgery, it’s now possible for almost every patient to have implants firmly anchored in the bone. If there’s insufficient bone in the jaw, augmentation under anesthesia is necessary. This can be done using:
the patient’s own bone
synthetic bone substitute materials
If there’s too little space in the sinus area, the sinus floor can be gently lifted via a sinus lift procedure.

By lifting the sinus floor, a small cavity is created above the jawbone. This space is then filled with bone grafts or substitutes, which harden within about four months. This method ensures the required stability for implants in the upper jaw (sinus lifts are only performed in the upper jaw).

Our team of experienced dentists and specially trained oral surgeons and implantologists will advise you on your individual situation. Planning your dental implants — from material selection to bone augmentation — is done jointly by your treating dentist and implantologist. Our in-house dental lab is also integrated into the planning process.
ALL Experts Under ONE Roof

In particularly complex cases, we offer 3D imaging to make sure nearby anatomical structures such as neighboring teeth, sinus cavities, and nerves are included in the planning. Your advantage: all specialists work together under one roof, right here in our Berlin dental practice. You won’t need to see any additional doctors during the planning phase.
Pain-free Tooth Replacement Thanks TO Anesthesia

For your comfort during longer procedures, our dental practice in Berlin has a dedicated surgical area and offers twilight sedation or general anesthesia. We take particular care with anxious patients and strive to make your entire experience — before, during, and after surgery — as pleasant as possible.
Preventive Implant Diagnostics AT KU64 – A Rarity IN Berlin Dental Practices

To ensure optimal implant placement, we recommend diagnostic testing in advance with our specialist for oral and maxillofacial surgery Dr. Jan Wagner or our oral surgeon Dr. Surian Herrmann. Implant diagnostics involve assessing immunological (inflammatory), osteological (bone-related), and genetic risks that could jeopardize long-term implant success. Modern preventive medicine makes it possible to identify risk patients early and develop personalized treatment plans.
Frequently Asked Questions About Dental Implants
Can the body develop an allergy to titanium implants?
Titanium contains no allergens and is neutral in the body. It’s therefore ideal for professional dental implants.
Who is a candidate for dental implants?
Bone growth should be complete — typically by age 18. There’s no upper age limit for dental implants.
Is the implant procedure done on an outpatient basis?
Yes, the procedure is performed under local anesthesia. Multiple implants can also be placed at once.
Will health insurance cover the costs?
In most cases, statutory health insurance does not cover implant treatment. However, a fixed subsidy may apply. In rare cases, full coverage is possible if medically justified.
How long does the treatment take?
The process includes around five appointments. Healing takes 8–12 weeks, followed by exposure of the implant and impression-taking. The final restoration is typically placed after four to six months.
Will I be without teeth during healing?
No. Removable dentures are adjusted or provisional solutions are provided during healing.
Is a local anesthetic enough?

Yes. The procedure is painless, though some pressure or vibration may be felt. For patients who prefer to sleep through it, general anesthesia is available — Wednesdays at KU64 Berlin, with consultations on Mondays from 5–6 p.m.
What other anesthesia options exist?
In addition to local anesthesia, general anesthesia and twilight sedation are available. Sedation puts you in a sleep-like state without full unconsciousness and allows quicker recovery.
Are implants suitable for diabetics?
Yes, provided diabetes is well-managed. Patients should consult their primary care physician beforehand.
Do implants set off airport security alarms?
No, implants are not magnetic. If needed, show your implant ID card.
What do implants feel like?
Give yourself and your new teeth some time. The implant has no nerves and may feel different at first. You’ll adjust within about six months.
Any issues with pacemakers?
No, dental implants don’t emit electromagnetic signals.
Will I be on sick leave?
You may be temporarily off work, but recovery is usually quick.
Are there interactions with medications?
Yes, medications like cortisone or blood thinners may require adjustments. Please inform us in advance.
Are there risks with implantation?
Yes, it’s a minor surgery. Nerve or vessel injury is possible, but rare. 3D imaging helps minimize risks. Rejection is extremely uncommon.
Will it hurt?
You may experience a mild wound sensation. Most discomfort is easily managed with over-the-counter pain relief. Severe pain is very rare.
Should I bleach my teeth before implantation?
Yes. Always whiten your natural teeth first to ensure the implant color matches perfectly.
Can I exercise after the procedure?
Avoid strenuous activities for the first few days.
How much do implants cost?
Costs vary based on the complexity and number of implants. We’ll provide a detailed treatment and cost plan free of charge.
How should I care for my teeth after implantation?
Brush as usual and use rinses. Titanium and ceramic implants are highly durable.
What is immediate implantation?
This is when an implant is placed immediately after a tooth is extracted.
What are alternatives to dental implants?
Root canal treatments or apicoectomies can preserve a non-vital tooth temporarily. However, implants are often the long-term solution.

eintraege.h1: Dental Implant Costs: What Does A Dental Implant Cost?

bloecke.text: A patient in need of dental prosthetics will likely start considering the costs of dental implants early on. One of the main advantages of implants over other types of dental restorations is their long lifespan, but this comes at a corresponding price. The cost of implants depends on many factors, which will be explained in detail below. Therefore, it is not possible to make general statements about the actual costs of individual dental implants at this point. However, we can provide insights into how implant costs are structured and what factors influence the price. Overall costs largely depend on the scope of the treatment, the type of dental implants, and the materials used.
Dental Implants: Costs AND HOW They ARE Structured

Logically, the cost of dental implants is heavily influenced by the complexity and effort involved in the implantation process and whether bone reconstruction (e.g., a sinus lift) is necessary beforehand. However, the initially high costs of implants should be considered in relation to their longevity and high success rate. When you consider that 90% of implants are typically still fully intact 10 years later, the price for a worry-free dental restoration becomes more reasonable, especially since, unlike with a standard bridge, no healthy teeth need to be replaced. The prices for a dental implant treatment cannot be quoted universally because the cost of an implant is made up of many different factors. Naturally, material costs for the dental implant depend on the type of implant material, as well as costs for surgical supplies, drills, and potentially necessary bone substitute material. If bone reconstruction is needed because the implant will not find sufficient stability in the jawbone, this will increase the price as well. Therefore, to specifically determine the cost of a dental implant, an initial consultation with the dentist is the first step.

The cost of dental implants is thus not solely a matter of materials. Also important are the fees for the implantologist, who is involved in all steps of the process, including diagnostics, planning, the actual implantation, the placement of the dental restoration, and any necessary bone reconstruction or sinus lift. The cost may seem high initially. However, it should be considered that the quality of dental implants should not be compromised to ensure long-term compatibility and durability. An experienced expert ensures that the implants remain intact for years to come and that the artificial tooth stays in place.

Additionally, the costs for dental technology or the dental laboratory, including the production of a 3D drilling template, are factored into the final implant costs. Since our practice has its own fully equipped dental laboratory, you save additional costs that would otherwise arise, for example, from shipping your implant. Of course, the type of dental restoration the patient desires plays a role. High-quality ceramic teeth look especially realistic but are more expensive than cheaper alternatives. The rule here is that a good tooth should not only look natural but also be made from durable materials.
In short, the cost of implants depends on the following factors:
Possibly bone reconstruction (e.g., sinus lift) and bone substitute material
The material of the dental implants (e.g., titanium)
The material of the dental restoration (e.g., ceramic for ceramic implants)
Surgical supplies for the implant procedure
The implantologist’s fee for their services (diagnostics, implantation, etc.)
The production of implants in the dental laboratory

The price can also differ depending on whether you need an implant for a back tooth or a front tooth. Implants for front teeth are slightly more expensive because aesthetic factors must be taken into account. For example, it is less critical if the transition from the silver-colored implant to the crown is slightly visible in a molar of the upper jaw than in a front incisor. If you have any questions about the cost of dental implants, we are happy to offer a comprehensive and non-binding consultation. Feel free to request a quote from us.
Dental Implants: HOW Much OF THE Cost IS Covered BY Health Insurance?

How much of the cost of dental implants will be covered depends on your insurance status. With a special supplementary dental insurance for implants, the costs may be partially or fully covered. On the other hand, statutory health insurance does not cover the full cost of dental implants. However, this does not mean that members of statutory health insurance must bear the entire cost themselves. For those with statutory insurance, there is a fixed subsidy for dental prosthetics, depending on the jaw situation. However, this subsidy applies only to the dental restoration placed on the implant (e.g., crown), not to the implant itself. The quality of the restoration also plays a role. High-quality ceramic implants, which look especially natural, are more expensive.

In addition to advice from your treating implantologist and dentist, our administrative staff, who regularly update their knowledge on current insurance reimbursement changes, will provide you with a personalized treatment and cost plan for your dental implants. We work closely with all major statutory health insurance providers and, if you have any questions about reimbursement, will also liaise directly with your private or statutory health insurer. Dental Implant Costs Abroad: Saving Money AT THE Expense OF Quality?

To save on implant costs, the trend is increasingly for patients to have implants placed abroad. In particular, Eastern European countries are popular for dental implants as providers there offer lower prices compared to Germany. However, patients should consider that the quality of the dental implants cannot be guaranteed to the same extent as in Germany and that this process carries certain risks. If you still want to have an implant placed abroad, it’s essential to gather information about the quality of the offering beforehand. Does the implant offer include bone reconstruction? Is this covered by the price? Is the material used of high quality? Who is the manufacturer of the dental implants? Do the dentists have qualifications comparable to those in Germany? What is the quality of medical care before and after surgery? All these questions should be clarified in advance, and online reviews can help assess whether you can fully trust implants from abroad. A comparison, including price comparisons, with domestic providers of implants is always a good idea.

To be fully safe in terms of implant quality and service, it is advisable to consult a German-standard certified expert for dental implants. These dentists and implantologists guarantee a worry-free implant procedure, with increasingly affordable implant costs. Providers who handle the production of dental implants and restorations, the placement of the prosthesis in the jaw, and the follow-up treatment all under one roof can offer patients reasonably priced service with high quality. At KU64, we offer all these services under one roof at our location in Berlin Charlottenburg. Implant production, placement, and aftercare are all provided at the most affordable prices possible, ensuring that the costs of dental implants won’t overshadow your joy with your new teeth.
Implants, Crowns, Dental Restoration – A Glossary

As a patient, it can be difficult to distinguish between the various forms of dental restorations. Terms are often used interchangeably, even when they refer to entirely different procedures. These procedures not only vary in the type of dental restoration but also in terms of cost. To avoid confusion between terms like dental implants, dental restorations, and crowns and bridges, here is a glossary:

Dental Restoration : Dental restoration is the general term for all forms of artificial teeth. These can include traditional dentures, various types of crowns, or more complex dental implants. The effort, durability, and costs of a dental restoration vary, as does the procedure used to place them.

Dental Implant : A dental implant is an artificial tooth (prosthesis) placed in the jawbone. Implants are typically made of titanium (a non-magnetic and biocompatible metal) and serve as artificial tooth roots. Implants can be placed in both the lower and upper jaw. There are various types of dental implants for different situations, each with different costs.

Bone Reconstruction : Depending on the implant system, bone reconstruction may be required. This occurs when the implant cannot be sufficiently anchored in the jawbone. Specialized materials are used to „build up" the jaw, allowing the dental implant to securely fit. Bone reconstruction incurs additional costs in implant treatment.

Crown : A crown (or implant crown) is the visible part of the implant designed to resemble a natural tooth. Ceramic is typically used (for ceramic implants), as it is strong, durable, and looks very natural. Depending on the quality and appearance of the crown, costs for the patient can vary.

Fixed Dental Restoration : Depending on the implant system, there is the option of either fixed or removable implants in the jaw. Fixed implants are primarily used for single-tooth implants, where the crown and artificial root are permanently bonded.

Removable Dental Restoration : Removable dental implants are implants where the ceramic crown is not permanently attached to the titanium implant. This is achieved with methods like the telescopic prosthesis, which is common for full implants.

eintraege.h1: Dental Implants: What Smokers Should Know Before the Procedure

bloecke.text: Smoking not only harms blood vessels, the heart, and lungs—it also poses a risk to dental, gum, and jaw health. For heavy smokers (over 20 cigarettes per day), getting and maintaining a dental implant comes with certain risks. Here we’ve outlined the most important facts about dental implants for smokers .
Dental Implants AND Smokers: Reduced Bone Stability

Scientific studies show that heavy smokers are six times more likely to develop inflammatory diseases of the periodontium (periodontitis) than non-smokers. This leads to the deterioration of jawbone and connective tissue in the oral cavity.

Aside from genetic factors, smokers often have poorer bone quality than non-smokers, which can make implant placement more difficult. A stable bone structure is essential for dental implants to ensure they are securely anchored. If bone volume is insufficient, surgical bone augmentation procedures—such as a sinus lift—may be required. These come with added risks for smokers. Our dental implant specialists recommend quitting smoking in advance if you want your implant to last long-term.
Smoking Delays Healing After Implant Surgery

If you decide to get a dental implant despite smoking, it’s important to understand that the procedure is complex. Unlike conventional restorations like crowns, implant placement is a surgical procedure. It involves opening the gum and preparing the jawbone at the selected site using a drill. The implant, usually designed with a screw thread, is then inserted into the bone.

Once successfully placed, the implant fuses naturally with the jawbone over the next three to six months, forming a firm base like a natural tooth root. Smoking during this healing phase can disrupt the process. Tobacco smoke contains harmful substances that increase inflammation in the mouth and hinder healing. For this reason, our implantology experts strongly advise against smoking after implant surgery.
Higher Risk OF Implant Loss IN Smokers
Even after the healing phase, smoking continues to affect the success of your dental implant. Studies have shown that implants have a shorter lifespan in smokers than in non-smokers.

A study by the University of Manchester found that smokers are twice as likely to lose implants within five years compared to non-smokers. In the study, 1,500 patients were observed (1,100 non-smokers and 549 smokers). Implant loss rates were 2.9% for non-smokers and 5.5% for smokers over five years. Other studies have shown that roughly 10% of smokers lose their implants within ten years.

One major cause of this increased failure rate is peri-implantitis—inflammation of the tissue surrounding the implant, which is more common among smokers. If left untreated, this inflammation can lead to implant loss, making the cost and effort of an implant all the more frustrating.
From GUM TO Hypnosis: Support FOR Quitting Smoking

The implantologists at KU64 Berlin recommend quitting smoking at least 14 days before and after both the bone graft and the implant procedure. Even better would be to quit permanently. Nicotine patches can help relieve withdrawal symptoms. Acupuncture or hypnotherapy with a qualified practitioner may also support smoking cessation.

However, dentists advise against replacing cigarettes with nicotine gums or lozenges after implant placement. Even though they don’t produce combustion residues like cigarette smoke, they still expose teeth, oral mucosa, and gums to the toxic effects of nicotine. This increases the risk of gum inflammation, periodontitis, and infections such as peri-implantitis or mucositis. In the long term, maintaining a good intake of vitamin C can help promote oral health. Our dental experts are happy to advise you on additional therapies to support smoking cessation.
Benefits OF Quitting Smoking FOR Your Health
Thinking about quitting smoking in preparation for your implant? Becoming a non-smoker protects your health and offers multiple benefits:
A brighter smile : Protect your new implant and enjoy a fresh, stain-free smile. Yellow discoloration on teeth, lips, or tongue becomes a thing of the past.
Healthier teeth : Non-smokers are less prone to cavities and typically accumulate less tartar than smokers.
Fewer inflammations and pain : Smoking heightens sensitivity in the mouth. Quitting reduces the risk of gum inflammation, periodontitis, and painful exposed tooth roots.
Stronger teeth : Inflammation of the gums and tooth-supporting structures weakens your dental foundation—leading to tooth loss. Quitting smoking helps preserve your natural support structures.
Fresher breath : Smoking fosters bacteria that cause bad breath. Quitting reduces these bacteria and helps maintain fresh breath.
Lower cancer risk : Smoking increases the risk of developing oral, throat, and laryngeal cancer. The good news: quitting gradually reduces this risk over time.
Even after years of smoking—it’s never too late to quit. The benefits of being smoke-free are often noticeable immediately and long-lasting.

Are you a smoker considering dental implants? We’re happy to advise you on your options for long-lasting implants and the right care for your restoration. You’ll find news and updates about our dental practice services on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and LinkedIn.

Call us at +49308647320, send us an email, or book your consultation directly with our dental implant expert Pablo Gonzales. Our dental clinic is open seven days a week.
Source : Press Office of the German Association for Implantology (DGI e.V.)
F.A.Q.
What IS Peri-implantitis?

Nicotine is a neurotoxin and constricts blood vessels. This impairs blood circulation in the oral cavity—especially in the gums—and weakens the immune system. As a result, an ideal breeding ground for bacteria is created. These bacteria can spread more easily and trigger inflammation around the neck of the dental implant and surrounding tissue, potentially even reaching the jawbone. Peri-implantitis is irreversible and leads to bone loss. If left untreated, it can result in the loss of dental implants and even adjacent healthy teeth. What’s more, peri-implantitis can still develop many years after implants have been placed.
HOW CAN I Prevent Peri-implantitis AS A Smoker?

Regular dental check-ups and professional cleanings are key to preventing peri-implantitis. Our implantology team is trained to detect and treat early signs of infection around implants. Be sure to inform your dentist that you smoke during your regular check-up.

In some adult patients, the jaws are positioned incorrectly in relation to each other. A satisfactory correction in these cases is often only possible through a combined orthodontic–maxillofacial surgical treatment.

During this treatment, the jaws are surgically repositioned to their correct alignment. This complex operation is performed exclusively by experienced oral and maxillofacial surgeons in a hospital setting and takes between 3 and 6 hours.

An orthodontic pretreatment is required before the surgery to shape and align the dental arches. After the operation, both jaws are fixed with wires for about one week, and the patient can only eat and drink through a straw during this period. About 3–4 weeks later, fine orthodontic adjustments begin.

Jaw repositioning will alter your facial appearance. Please be aware that your facial features will change as a result of the procedure. Some patients have always wished for this change, while for others it can be a challenge.

When your teeth fall out of line, the orthodontists at KU64 in Berlin are here to help. Whether it’s crooked or crowded teeth or a gap in your smile, we’ll help you achieve a healthy bite and a radiant, natural smile.

Your Orthodontist IN Berlin – FOR Every AGE

You’re never too old for straight teeth and a confident smile. That’s why KU64 in Berlin offers personalized treatments to correct tooth and jaw misalignments – for children, teens and adults alike. As long as your teeth are well-anchored in the jawbone, orthodontic treatment is possible at 30, 40 or even 50. Treatment for adults may just take a little longer than it does for younger patients.
THE Consequences OF Misaligned Teeth
Tooth and jaw misalignments can affect your entire health and are often the cause of chronic health conditions, such as:
Digestive issues caused by poor chewing function
Postural problems and resulting back pain
Jaw misalignment
Headaches due to muscle tension
Protruding teeth – especially vulnerable in case of falls
Crowded teeth that are difficult to clean, increasing the risk of tooth decay and gum disease
Deep bites that may damage the tooth-supporting structures
Crossbites that can lead to facial asymmetry and imbalances throughout the body
With the right orthodontic treatment – such as braces – our Berlin-based team can help prevent these health issues from developing in the first place.
Straight Teeth: Your Personal Calling Card

Healthy teeth and a beautiful smile are part of everyone’s first impression. When you meet someone, their gaze naturally falls on your face – so why not take the opportunity to correct a misalignment? Clean, straight teeth and a confident smile contribute greatly to a friendly, well-groomed appearance and boost your self-esteem at any age. Especially with nearly invisible braces like Invisalign®, there’s no reason to hold back your smile.
Your Trusted Orthodontist
Only an orthodontist or a dentist with orthodontic expertise can determine whether treatment is needed for functional or aesthetic reasons.
Holistic AND Individual: THE KU64 Treatment Plan

Orthodontists need to see the whole person – and at KU64 Berlin, we embrace a holistic concept of care. Every set of teeth is unique, and so is every treatment plan. That’s why tailored therapy is essential to successful outcomes. Our orthodontic team takes time to carefully assess your dental and jaw structure through a comprehensive consultation and diagnostic exam.
Diagnostic Assessment: Essential FOR Success

Diagnosis includes a full medical and dental history, clinical exams, dental impressions, X-rays and photographs. We also assess your overall posture, tongue positioning, muscle function and breathing patterns. Based on these insights, your orthodontist will decide whether treatment is advisable – and if so, our experts will create a customized treatment plan tailored to your needs.
When Should YOU SEE AN Orthodontist?
Tooth and jaw misalignments can impact your overall health. The dentists at KU64 Berlin recommend orthodontic treatment in cases such as:
Overbite – Upper front teeth extend too far over the lower teeth
Underbite – Lower teeth protrude too far forward or upper teeth are too far back
Open bite – Gaps between upper and/or lower front or back teeth when the jaws are closed
Midline asymmetry – Misalignment of the center lines of upper and lower front teeth
Spacing – Gaps caused by missing teeth or undersized teeth
Crowding – Not enough space in the jaw for all teeth
Braces: Your Nearly Invisible Companion FOR A Brighter Smile

Braces used to have a bad reputation – especially metal wires that sparkle in professional settings. But things have changed: correcting crooked teeth no longer means you need fixed, visible braces. Today, children, teens and adults can choose from a wide variety of braces – fixed or removable, visible or invisible. These devices apply gentle pressure to reposition teeth and jaws, retrain muscles, and influence jaw growth.

Your orthodontist will determine which method is most suitable depending on your specific case. Our team in Berlin-Charlottenburg will explain all the options – including advantages, features and costs – for children, teens and adults. By the way: braces can also help with snoring therapy, using special oral appliances known as mandibular advancement devices.
Multi-bracket Appliances

The best-known type of braces are multi-bracket appliances (fixed braces), consisting of brackets, bands and wires. Bands are attached to the back teeth and act as anchors, while brackets are usually bonded to the front of each tooth. At our Berlin-Charlottenburg practice, we work with the DAMON Q+ and DAMON Clear systems for fixed orthodontic treatments.
Invisalign®

Tooth correction doesn’t always require traditional braces. Invisalign® is an excellent option for closing gaps, straightening crooked front teeth, or widening narrow dental arches. Our orthodontists create two clear, removable aligners (so-called „aligners") that gradually move your teeth into place. Every two weeks, the aligners are replaced with a new set to guide teeth toward the desired final position.
Retainers

After active treatment, retainers help preserve the new position of your teeth. They are available as removable or fixed devices and are typically worn for one to two years post-treatment. Whether you need brackets, Invisalign®, Spark (Ormco), or WIN – our team at KU64 Berlin will recommend the ideal solution from our orthodontic range.

From Metal Brackets, Ceramic Brackets & More

We would like to inform you about the various types of fixed braces and the process of orthodontic treatment at the KU64 dental practice. A multi-bracket appliance (MB) – the fixed brace – consists of brackets and bands that the orthodontist adheres to the teeth to be moved. These teeth are then connected by an archwire, which applies force to the teeth through its elastic tendency to return to its original shape, moving the tooth into the correct position.
THE Brackets OF A Brace

The materials used by the orthodontist for fixed braces with brackets range from unprogrammed stainless steel brackets to nearly invisible ceramic brackets. Brackets can also be applied to the inner surface of the teeth, making the fixed braces completely undetectable. In some cases, the orthodontist has the option to use conventional materials to create a virtually invisible brace. However, for those who want a truly invisible brace, we recommend learning more about „Invisalign," which is also offered by our practice.
Braces with Stainless Steel Brackets

With unprogrammed stainless steel brackets (also known as metal brackets), the archwire is held in place by an elastic ring or fine wires (ligatures). These brackets are quite large, and cleaning between the rubber rings or ligatures can be challenging.
Braces with Mini Brackets
Mini brackets require less bonding surface on the teeth, making them less noticeable and creating less of a foreign body sensation in the mouth compared to traditional braces.
Braces with SL Brackets

Self-ligating brackets (SL brackets, Damon Q) feature a small flap that holds the archwire in place within the bracket slot. The archwire is not held by elastic rings or wires. The advantage of braces with self-ligating brackets is that the archwire can glide freely within the slot, overcoming no friction resistance. This results in more efficient force transmission and a shorter orthodontic treatment time. Self-ligating brackets are available in both metal and ceramic versions.
Braces with Ceramic Brackets

Ceramic brackets are tooth-colored and less noticeable (Damon Clear). The material is more brittle and harder. As a result, patients may experience wear on their teeth if they bite into a ceramic bracket. In some cases, ceramic brackets must be carefully ground down during the removal of the braces.
THE Archwires OF A Brace
Archwires are categorized into steel wires and super-elastic or thermoelastic wires.
Steel Archwires vs. Super-Elastics in Braces

Steel archwires are easy to bend but fatigue quickly, reducing the force they apply on the teeth. For this reason, super-elastic archwires were developed in orthodontics. These archwires cannot be bent, but they offer high spring force. They apply a very small but continuous force on the tooth over an extended period. This protects the tissue and facilitates necessary bone remodeling. The risk of side effects, such as root damage, is significantly reduced. At the same time, treatment time can be drastically shortened.

The forces exerted by modern super-elastic archwires on the tooth-supporting structures are within a range considered gentle to the teeth by modern orthodontics. Therefore, many disadvantages of traditional braces are no longer observed today. With the use of the latest materials and consideration of current medical standards, modern fixed braces do not harm the teeth or the supporting structures. The use of the latest techniques and materials has been standard in our practice since its inception. However, appropriate at-home oral hygiene remains essential.

No matter which of the many brace options available at our practice you choose in consultation with your orthodontist, you’re making a great choice. Straight teeth and a charming smile can greatly enhance your quality of life.

At KU64 dental practice, our orthodontists offer the crystal-clear, nearly invisible Invisalign® aligners, providing significantly more comfort than traditional braces. Benefits OF Invisalign®:
nearly invisible appearance
removable, e.g., before important appointments
easy hygiene—thanks to flexibility and absence of metal wires, teeth can be brushed and flossed regularly with Invisalign®
comfortable to wear
overlapping teeth can be corrected without brackets and wires—even for minor misalignments
suitable for teenagers and adults
smile whenever and as much as you like
HOW Does Invisalign® Work?

Similar to conventional braces, when opting for Invisalign®, we initially take photos, x-rays, and dental impressions at our practice to create a treatment plan. These data are sent to the manufacturer Align Technology, who converts them into a 3D digital representation. This allows our orthodontists to simulate the entire treatment process in 3D, visualizing the planned results individually. In other words, with Invisalign® technology, your smile can also become a „designer smile"!
Using Invisalign® FOR Teenagers AND Adults

Once we have virtually planned your treatment with you, you can view your dental alignment process in a 3D animation. Based on the gathered data, a series of clear „aligners" (from English „to align" – „straighten," „arrange") is custom-made. Invisalign® aligners are manufactured separately for the upper and lower jaw from lightweight plastic material, fitting precisely onto your teeth. Each Invisalign® aligner set is worn for at least two weeks, then replaced by a new set that slightly differs from the previous ones—thus gently moving your teeth into the desired position. You’ll be proud of the results and your new smile!

The duration of treatment with Invisalign® invisible aligners is determined by our dentists and orthodontists at the beginning of the treatment and varies in length and cost depending on the complexity of your specific case. Typically, Invisalign® treatment lasts six to 18 months.

Daily wear: 22 hours. Invisalign® aligners should only be removed during meals and oral hygiene. Approximately every two to three weeks, new aligners are provided (per jaw) until the treatment goal is achieved. Afterward, as with fixed braces, we recommend a retainer to maintain the results achieved with Invisalign® permanently.

Invisalign® aligners are also suitable for teenagers from the age of eleven who no longer have primary teeth, though teeth may still be erupting. This is accounted for in the aligner design. Invisalign® also delivers particularly effective results for recurrent, partial orthodontic treatments and crowded teeth, where not all teeth require fixed braces.

Adjustment period: It takes only a few days; afterward, Invisalign® is generally well tolerated. For teenagers (tailored Invisalign Teen® treatment), a color indicator shows whether the aligner has been worn for the required hours or days.

KU64 dental practice is an official Invisalign® provider and has achieved Platinum status for extensive use of the Invisalign® method. We’re happy to explain exactly how Invisalign® works! Contact us with any questions about Invisalign® treatment. Our orthodontists will gladly assist you, including with questions not answered in the Invisalign® FAQ!

eintraege.h1: Before Your Child's First Visit AT KU64

bloecke.text: Tips for Parents – How to best prepare your child for their first dentist visit
Dear Parents,

It’s our heartfelt wish that your child arrives with a smile and leaves our practice smiling as well. That’s why we’ve compiled this brief guide with tips to help you best prepare your child for their first dentist visit:
Please try announcing the dentist appointment cheerfully from the very beginning: a. Saying „Yes! Today you get to visit the dentist!" sets a positive mood,
b. „Oh dear, today we have to take you to the dentist!" creates negativity from the outset, as fears from parents can easily transfer to children.

Only speak positively about your own dental experiences. If you don’t have positive experiences, it’s better not to mention them. Make it clear to your child that negative stories from others shouldn’t be taken seriously and discuss these at home.

Avoid negatively loaded words like fear, pain, hurt, drilling, injection, and similar terms, including negations of them. Sentences like „You don’t need to be afraid, it won’t hurt," cause the subconscious mind to register only „afraid" and „hurt," introducing the idea that something bad might happen at the dentist. Similarly, statements like „You need to be very brave!" create negative expectations.

False promises cause distrust. Statements like „You won’t feel a thing" or „It’ll be quick" unfortunately can’t always be kept. Even gentle and painless treatments will still be noticed, and a thorough examination or careful therapy can take longer than „just quick." Young children lack a real sense of time, and such promises can only disappoint them and us as pediatric dentists!

Promises of rewards make your child think something terrible is coming, as large rewards are often associated with negative experiences. Feeling they must earn something increases stress beforehand. Even phrases like „Mommy will hold your hand" suggest comfort will be necessary.

Helpful explanations like „Your dentist will count your teeth today and see if they’re all healthy" are ideal. The first visit involves no treatment; we will prepare your child for anything beyond that. If pain is the reason for the first visit, say something like: „Your dentist will help you feel better today."

Children’s books about „visiting the dentist" are also great preparation. They illustrate what to expect. You can also role-play the dentist situation at home using stuffed animals or favorite toys to help your child practice.
If your child isn’t very young, encourage them to enter the treatment room alone. Experience shows this often works better.
Let your child answer our questions, so they feel and know they’re at the center of attention.
Praise your child after the appointment. This builds self-confidence and motivates them to try new things.
Make the first dentist visit a positive experience!
Please keep in mind that at our KU64 Youngstars Club things might differ from your childhood experiences. A child-friendly, pain-free treatment is our highest priority!

Registration Form and Risk Assessment Questionnaire

Before your first dental examination, we’ll ask you to fill out a registration form. These details help identify risk factors early and prevent complications. You’ll receive the form from our dental assistants upon arrival.

Please inform us if you regularly or currently take medications. Your medication pass or the package insert of your medication helps us predict potential interactions.

eintraege.h1: Innovative Pediatric Orthodontics FOR Children AND Adolescents

bloecke.text: What IS THE Purpose OF Pediatric Orthodontics?

Pediatric orthodontics focuses on preventing and treating dental and jaw misalignments in children. These often cause chronic health problems (e.g., digestive issues due to poor chewing function, posture problems resulting in back pain, misaligned jaws, tension-related headaches, etc.).

For example, protruding teeth are especially vulnerable to injury from falls or impacts. Crowded teeth are difficult to clean, potentially leading to cavities and gum disease. A deep bite can damage the tooth-supporting structures. Incorrect bite function (e.g., crossbite) may cause facial asymmetry and imbalance throughout the body. Early detection and correction of these misalignments are therefore particularly important for children. Due to these factors, orthodontists must always take a holistic view—something we strive to achieve at KU64 through our comprehensive therapeutic concept.
When IS Orthodontic Treatment Necessary FOR Your Child?

Only a dentist or orthodontist can determine whether orthodontic treatment is necessary. For diagnosis, a complete medical and dental history, clinical examination, dental impressions, specialized X-rays, and photographs are required. Based on this information, the orthodontist or pediatric dentist can decide whether orthodontic treatment is advisable and, if so, develop the appropriate treatment plan.
Orthodontics FOR Primary (baby) Teeth:

Indications at this stage include open bites caused by thumb-sucking that impair biting function, crossbites that could inhibit jaw growth, premature loss of baby teeth, and severe crowding preventing permanent teeth from growing properly. Simple, typically removable appliances worn by children in the afternoon and at night can have significant positive effects, improve body posture (see also holistic orthodontics), and thus enhance your child’s well-being. Typically, active plates and functional orthodontic appliances are used.
Removable appliances (also called functional orthodontic devices) include:
the Activator for protruding lower jaws (Class III),
the Bionator for receding lower jaws, deep bites, or open bites,
the Elastically-Open Activator (EOA) for open bites,
and the Fränkel Functional Regulator III (FR III) for prognathism (lower jaw protrudes beyond upper jaw).
All four appliances help correct growth anomalies and jaw misalignments during developmental stages.
However, when using removable orthodontic appliances, cooperation and support from parents are often necessary to ensure consistent use by the child.
Orthodontics During THE Mixed Dentition Phase:

In most cases, starting orthodontic treatment (fixed or removable appliances, such as Invisalign) at the onset of the second tooth eruption—usually around the age of 9–10—is sufficient. At this time, an examination by our specialists is recommended to determine the most suitable treatment. The goal is to create space for all permanent teeth, establish the correct alignment between jaws to prevent temporomandibular joint issues and back pain, and position all permanent teeth correctly in the jawbone.

Proper aesthetics naturally result from achieving correct function. Here, we use removable braces, functional orthodontic devices, fixed appliances placed either internally (Incognito) or externally, and transparent aligners (Invisalign).
IF Your Child Shows ANY OF THE Following Misalignments, Parents Should Seek AN Orthodontic Evaluation:
Overbite – Upper front teeth protrude excessively over the lower teeth.
Underbite – Lower teeth are positioned too far forward, or upper teeth too far back.
Open bite – A gap between the edges of the front teeth and/or the chewing surfaces of the back teeth when biting together.
Misaligned midline – The centers of the upper and lower front teeth do not align.
Spacing – Gaps or spaces due to missing teeth or teeth not occupying the entire jaw.
Crowding – Insufficient space in the jaw ridge for all teeth.
Everything FOR A Healthy Child's Smile!

Every set of teeth is as unique as its owner. Thus, an individualized, tailored treatment plan and parental involvement are essential for successful treatment. Regular training and further education of our orthodontists and practice team guarantee expertise at the highest level and orthodontic treatments (including innovative methods like Incognito or Invisalign) that consider the whole person.
HOW Does THE Treatment Process Work IN Pediatric Orthodontics?

Many different appliances—both fixed and removable—can gently apply pressure to jaws and teeth, reposition teeth, retrain muscles, and influence jaw growth. Based on the type and severity of the problem, we determine which orthodontic treatment offers the greatest likelihood of success. A fixed appliance, such as a multi-bracket apparatus consisting of brackets, bands, or wires, may be used. Bands are attached to teeth and act as anchors, while brackets are typically bonded to the front surfaces of teeth.
Orthodontics AND Speech Therapy

Orthodontic treatment can be accompanied by speech therapy to harmonize tongue and muscle functions, or osteopathic treatment to positively influence bodily dysfunction, fascial tension, and postural issues.
Expertise AT ITS Best

Our dental specialists engage in continuous communication to create the optimal treatment plan for your child. Patients benefit from our unique concept of short pathways, excellent coordination among colleagues, and state-of-the-art technology. Advances in techniques and materials have enabled nearly metal-free and invisible braces, naturally used at KU64. We exclusively use tested, biocompatible materials and provide extended guarantees, far exceeding industry standards.
Everything Under ONE Roof
Our in-house, experienced dental lab ensures the highest quality and biocompatible materials.
Get in touch! Dr. Isabella Piekos, specialist orthodontist and dentist for holistic orthodontics and osteopathy, is pleased to advise you about all orthodontic treatments we offer at our practice!

eintraege.h1: Anesthesia – Pain-Free Treatment While Sleeping with General Anesthesia at the Dentist

bloecke.text: Anesthesia and General Sedation for Dental Procedures

At KU64, both you and your little ones have the option of simply “sleeping through” the treatment. Fear of dental procedures, extensive dental restorations, or surgical interventions are all valid reasons for undergoing treatment under anesthesia or sedation.

Some forms of anesthesia are administered directly by our dentists, while others are handled by trained anesthesiologists. We work closely with a trusted team of external anesthesia specialists who have been supporting us for many years – ensuring our patients receive the best possible care before, during, and after the procedure.
Our reception team will be happy to arrange your appointment.
Types of Anesthesia at KU64:
Topical anesthesia: Applied as a fruity-flavored gel, it numbs the area and makes the following injection feel almost painless.
Local anesthesia: Used to achieve complete pain relief in over 95% of cases.
Nitrous oxide (laughing gas): A great option for kids as well as anxious adult patients. It significantly reduces or eliminates the gag reflex and noticeably lowers pain sensitivity.

Twilight sedation (conscious sedation): A gentle intravenous “comfort cocktail,” usually Dormicum and Propofol, is administered. This method is less demanding on the body than general anesthesia, and you remain responsive – though you typically won’t remember the treatment afterward.

General anesthesia: Intubation anesthesia (ITN) is typically used for surgeries or pediatric treatments. Whether for a lengthy procedure or a short intervention, our anesthesiologists combine years of experience with the latest medical technology.
By the way:
If desired, we can even administer an antidote at the end of the treatment to help the numb feeling wear off more quickly!

eintraege.h1: Periodontics Berlin: Treat Periodontitis and Protect Your Teeth

bloecke.text: [ Fighting painful gum disease (periodontitis) ]
PERIODONTITIS in Berlin: Prevention, Treatment & Aftercare for Gum Disease

There is something you can do about gum inflammation and gum recession! Periodontitis (also known as periodontal disease or gingivitis) — the colloquial term for a gum infection that may lead to tooth loss — can be successfully treated by targeting its bacterial causes. At KU64 Berlin, our periodontics specialists provide systematic gum treatments tailored to your needs.

Patients who consult a dentist at an early stage of periodontitis (bacterial gum disease) can often avoid future tooth replacements such as implants, bridges, or crowns altogether. Gum treatment and consistent oral hygiene maintained by the patient are crucial for preserving natural teeth and may help avoid complex dental procedures.
Our dental hygienists and prophylaxis experts at KU64 Berlin are happy to advise you on preventive care for periodontitis!
Recognising Periodontal Disease

Although gum infections are widespread in Germany, they are rarely detected early. That’s because initial symptoms are usually mild and often not associated with a serious condition. Lack of awareness only adds to the problem.

Periodontitis is the most common form of gum disease — and is now a more frequent cause of tooth loss than cavities. Periodontics focuses on preserving or restoring gum health, ideally avoiding the need for artificial teeth. In some cases, high-quality implants remain the best solution.

Early diagnosis is especially important for implant patients. To ensure our prophylaxis program protects your implants effectively, we also assess your bone metabolism, which can be impacted by undetected diabetes or low vitamin D levels. We now offer tests for both.
Implant-Safe Test: €64
Vitamin D Test: €49
Diabetes Test: €49
Mention your interest during your next check-up appointment.
How Periodontitis Develops

More and more people suffer from chronic inflammation of the gums and supporting structures. It’s caused by bacteria found in dental plaque, which also contribute to tartar. These bacteria settle on the tooth root surface and move toward the root tip. The immune system then responds by attacking both the bacteria and the supporting tissues — eventually leading to tooth loosening and loss. Fortunately, early treatment can prevent this.
Prevention Is the Best Protection for Your Teeth

Inflammation of the gums or periodontal pockets (gingivitis or periodontitis) can be prevented with good oral hygiene and regular check-ups. Dentists can detect periodontitis early during a routine check-up or even during professional cleanings. Bleeding gums may be an early warning sign.
At our KU64 dental practice in Berlin, we are one of the few clinics offering the PerioSafe® Test — the world’s first diagnostic test for detecting hidden tissue loss in the gums.
Early signs of periodontitis / gingivitis or gum disease include:
(Note: These symptoms often go unnoticed due to the lack of pain.) – Dark red gums – Bleeding when touched – Mild swelling – Bad breath
Causes of Periodontitis

There are many causes of gum disease: poor oral hygiene, infrequent professional cleanings, nutritional deficiencies, aggressive bacteria, misaligned teeth or bite issues, immune system disorders, and genetic predisposition — all can contribute to periodontal damage and root sensitivity.
Innovative Laser Treatment with EmunDo®

While antibiotics are often used to treat periodontitis, laser therapy with EmunDo® is a highly effective alternative — especially in persistent cases. EmunDo® is a dye that, when activated by laser, targets and eliminates harmful bacteria without promoting antibiotic resistance. Safe, precise, and powerful — your health will thank you!
FAQs on Periodontitis
Periodontitis and Your General Health

Studies have shown links between periodontitis and serious conditions, such as: – Heart attack – Stroke – Premature birth – Chronic respiratory diseases – Intestinal disorders Also important: bad breath is often caused by byproducts of periodontitis bacteria.
Smoking and Periodontitis

As with general health, smoking worsens gum disease and negatively affects treatment outcomes. Smokers require even more intensive oral hygiene and will receive extra support from our KU64 dental hygiene team in Berlin.
Systematic Gum Treatment at KU64 Berlin
The goal of periodontal treatment is to remove bacteria from beneath the gumline and within gum pockets, eliminating the root cause of the inflammation.
The procedure is divided into four phases:

1. Pretreatment (2–3 sessions): All plaque above the gumline is removed both manually and mechanically. We’ll teach you how to maintain this clean state at home — your cooperation is essential for success.

2. Treatment (1–2 sessions): The actual periodontal therapy focuses on removing bacteria and calculus (tartar) from deep root surfaces, typically under local anesthesia. This is done using hand instruments, ultrasonic tools, medical rinses, and a special laser with a fluorescence-controlled feedback system that precisely vaporizes bacteria and calculus, sterilizing the pockets and stimulating healing.
Note: Some sensitivity to hot/cold or biting may occur temporarily — this is no cause for concern.

3. Possible Regeneration (Bone Reconstruction): In certain cases, lost bone and periodontal structures can be rebuilt using minimally invasive microsurgery and bioactive substances. Prerequisite: completed periodontal therapy and excellent oral hygiene.

4. Aftercare and Recall: Even after treatment, susceptibility to bacteria remains. That’s why regular professional cleanings and follow-up appointments are essential to keep gum disease from returning. These appointments typically occur every 1 to 3 months depending on disease severity and include antibacterial rinses to also protect against cavities.
Gum Grafting and Recession Coverage

Exposed roots don’t just affect your smile — they can also cause sensitivity. At KU64 Berlin, we use minimally invasive microsurgery with your own tissue to rebuild your gums, enhancing both health and appearance.
Minimally Invasive Periodontal Surgery

As the name implies, this gentle surgical approach minimizes pain, shortens recovery, and improves results. We use ultra-fine instruments, special sutures from vascular surgery, magnifying loupes, and an operating microscope.
Dental Implants and Periodontitis
If you’ve lost teeth due to periodontitis, implants can restore your smile without harming adjacent teeth. For successful implantation, two conditions must be met:
– Your periodontal treatment must be completed – Your oral hygiene must be excellent
Our hygiene team is happy to advise you further.
Bacterial and Saliva Testing for Periodontitis Risk
A bacterial analysis of deep gum pockets can help predict disease progression and guide antibiotic selection if needed.
Periodontitis and Gum Aesthetics

A beautiful smile depends on both white teeth and healthy pink gums. Thin or inflamed gums may recede and expose sensitive roots, disrupting the harmony of your smile. Our gum grafting procedures restore this balance — so you can smile with confidence again.
Gut Health and Periodontitis

What does your gut have to do with your gums? Many digestive disorders cause mineral and vitamin deficiencies, which are essential for gum and bone health. A weak gut also compromises your immune system, making it harder to fight inflammation. A gut cleanse can strengthen your immune defense — supporting periodontal healing.
Learn more about gut health at www.darmflora-analyse.de . We’ll be happy to advise you on holistic periodontitis treatment at KU64 and in collaboration with MDL.
Sinus Lift and Bone Augmentation for Dental Implants

For long-term implant success, sufficient bone is essential. If bone mass is lacking, augmentation procedures like sinus lifts can help. Bone loss may result from periodontitis, tooth loss, denture pressure, genetic factors, illnesses, medications, aging, or smoking.

What’s needed for bone augmentation? You need sufficient bone height and width. Width is easier to restore than height. In the lower jaw, bone density is typically better than in the upper jaw. If the upper jaw lacks bone due to the sinus cavity, a sinus lift may be required.
External vs. Internal Sinus Lift Both procedures thicken the floor of the sinus cavity:
– External sinus lift is more complex and is used when significant height must be gained. – Internal sinus lift is less invasive and uses the implant’s drill channel for access.
Our implantology specialists at KU64 Berlin will help determine which is right for you.
